title: Local operational audit records and `ward audit`
description: Spec §9.4. Admission recorded before delivery, completion separately; sanitized fields only; bounded retention stated, not hidden.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T19: a pre-delivery audit persistence failure blocks delivery; a post-delivery failure is reported without claiming rollback
`ward audit --json` shows only current-project sanitized events and states its retention bound

implementationNotes:
WCLI-10/WCLI-11 SPLIT, RULED BY OPUM-AGENT (2026-09-29, ~05:32Z). Written here before WCLI-10 lands, at the ruling's own instruction, so this task's successor does not rebuild what WCLI-10 already carries.

WHAT WCLI-10 OWNS, and will already exist when this task starts. The run path: admission persisted before a credential is delivered, delivery, completion persisted after in its own transaction. The audit itself is a REQUIRED INJECTED PORT (src/application/transport.ts is the shape to copy; the port's record type is domain/vault-state.ts's AuditRecord), wired to a minimal vault-backed recorder writing into the vault's auditRecords collection via withAuditRecord. Admission re-reads the binding, the approval and the secret inside its own transaction, which is where revocation's admission-time semantics live. There is no field in AuditRecord a value could be written into, deliberately: no credential, no request or response body, no upstream message. auditHistoryLimit in domain/vault-state.ts is currently 500, oldest dropped first, global across projects rather than per project.

WHAT IS THIS TASK'S, and is not done by WCLI-10. (1) `ward audit --json`: current-project sanitized events only, and it STATES its retention bound rather than leaving a reader to discover it. (2) The retention bound's own statement and any change to it: WCLI-10 set a bound so the collection could not grow unbounded, but it is WCLI-11's to expose and to justify. (3) The fuller field set spec 9.4 names and WCLI-10 deliberately left unpopulated - observed OS identity, and the optional explicitly self-asserted actor/task labels. (4) T19, both halves: a pre-delivery audit persistence FAILURE blocks delivery, and a post-delivery failure is REPORTED WITHOUT CLAIMING ROLLBACK. The mechanism for both exists in WCLI-10 (the admission write throwing blocks the run; the completion write's failure is caught and surfaced as auditRecorded:false with exit 6 while the outcome still reports the operation honestly) - what is owed here is the evidence at the vault, not the plumbing.

THE REASONING, recorded so it is not re-litigated. A `ward run` that delivered a credential without an admission record would violate spec 9.4, and a no-op audit port in a shipped build would be the decorative control opum-sdlc explicitly forbids - a control that occupies the slot and stops anyone looking for a real one. The split is WCLI-10 owns the run path's control flow and the port; WCLI-11 owns the viewing command, the stated bound, the field set and T19.

EVIDENCE ALREADY IN PLACE from WCLI-10 that this task can build on rather than re-derive: test/run.test.ts asserts the ordering directly - a fake transport reads the vault at the moment it is called and must see the admission record and only the admission record; a failing admission is asserted to leave the transport uncalled and the history empty; a failing completion is asserted to leave the transport called exactly once, the admission record written, and the result carrying outcome succeeded with auditRecorded false and exit 6.

RECYCLE HANDOFF, written at a coherent boundary (2026-09-29, at opum-agent's renewal order). WCLI-11 IS NOT STARTED - zero implementation, zero branch. This note adds a survey and a plan; it does not restate the SPLIT note already on this record, which is still correct and should be read first.

WCLI-10 IS DONE, MERGED AND PROMOTED. Squash 58d0604 on dev, promoted to main, verified: origin/main^{tree} equals origin/dev^{tree} and main is an ancestor of dev. So everything the SPLIT note says "will already exist when this task starts" now exists, and can be read rather than assumed. WCLI-15's dependency list now names WCLI-10 (0d6f6b6), which is why this task is ready.

WHAT WAS SURVEYED, so the successor does not re-derive it. A read-only command in this repo is three touches, not one: the command is declared in src/contract/manifest.ts (name, kind, outputSensitivity, examples - see the status entry near line 176), dispatched through the handlers record in src/application/commands.ts, and implemented beside its siblings in src/application/reporting.ts, where runStatus and runDoctor are the template. test/contract.test.ts asserts the manifest and the handler set agree, so a command declared without a handler is a red build rather than a runtime surprise.

THE PLAN, in the order I would do it.

(1) `ward audit --json`: current-project records only, and the retention bound STATED. This is the smaller half and it satisfies one acceptance criterion on its own, so it is a complete reviewable slice. It needs a current-project filter over state.auditRecords - the same projectId resolution the run path uses (boundProjectId in src/application/run.ts) - and it must carry auditHistoryLimit from src/domain/vault-state.ts:130 into the output rather than leaving a reader to find it.

A DESIGN POINT THAT WILL BITE AND IS NOT MINE TO SETTLE SILENTLY. auditHistoryLimit is 500 GLOBAL across projects, oldest dropped first, deliberately - the constant's own comment says a per-project bound would let one project's activity be pushed out by another's and would have to be enforced at every write to mean anything. But that means a project can see fewer than 500 of its own records, and the number it sees depends on other projects' activity. So "states its retention bound" has two candidate meanings: the global bound, or the effective bound for this project. Whoever does this should pick one, say which, and put the reasoning where the constant is - this is a question for opum-agent if it is not obvious from the spec, not a coin flip.

(2) The fuller field set spec 9.4 names and WCLI-10 left unpopulated: observed OS identity, and the optional explicitly self-asserted actor/task labels. FLAG BEFORE STARTING: this changes AuditRecord's shape, and the vault state parser validates an exact key set per record (see the secrets reader around src/domain/vault-state.ts:247, which compares Object.keys against a sorted expected list and calls malformed() on any difference). So adding fields is a vault-format change, not a struct edit - it interacts with vaultStateFormatVersion (vault-state.ts:30) and with the same bump-or-explain question WCLI-10 answered for profileSnapshotVersion, where the answer was written into the comment above the constant and filed as WCLI-38. Expect to make that call again here, and to record it the same way.

(3) T19, both halves, as EVIDENCE AT THE VAULT. The mechanism is WCLI-10's and is already tested at the run path: test/run.test.ts asserts a failing admission leaves the transport uncalled and the history empty, and a failing completion leaves the transport called exactly once, the admission present, outcome succeeded, auditRecorded false, exit 6. What is owed here is the vault-side evidence, not the plumbing - do not rebuild the recorder.

RAILS, unchanged. No test or probe touches the developer's real ~/.ward or its keychain item; everything runs against temporary stores, a memory credential store and throwaway checkouts. Publish nothing. WCLI-19, WCLI-31 and WCLI-37 are other tasks and none of them is a prerequisite here.

TWO ENVIRONMENT FACTS FOR THE SUCCESSOR. Disk was healthy at this boundary (485 GiB on /Volumes/external, 12 GiB on the system volume) but was at 100 percent twice on 2026-09-29 and DEC-17 is still open with the operator, so re-measure before claiming a full local gate ran. And .quest/ is committed and branch-scoped: a quest write is a read-modify-write of the BRANCH's copy, so merge origin/dev into a feature branch before the first tracker edit of a task, or the edit writes the record back without the notes dev has since added.

STATE AT THIS BOUNDARY, verified rather than remembered: dev is 1 commit ahead of main (the WCLI-15 dependency chore, 0d6f6b6, tracker-only). That promotion is an orchestrator decision and was not ordered, so it is left for whoever takes it. No open pull requests. No In Progress tasks. Local branches are dev and main only, both level with their origin refs. Cursor left in place deliberately: this session wrote it and is the one being recycled, so deleting it would remove the successor's only pointer (OPAG-678).

SKILLS for the successor: opum-sdlc (branch, PR, merge, promote), opum-handoff (restore), quest, lore.
